old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a family of swans on a calm body of water on a foggy day. The water is still, reflecting the muted colors of the surroundings, and the fog creates a soft, ethereal atmosphere. Initially, one adult swan is seen swimming, its white feathers contrasting sharply with the grayish-blue water. Two swan cygnets are also visible, their smaller size and darker plumage making them stand out against the adult. The adult swan occasionally dips its head, and the cygnets move minimally. The scene is static, with no discernible camera motion, and the fog envelops the background, creating a uniform, indistinct backdrop. The overall mood is peaceful, highlighting the natural presence of these birds in their environment.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a family of swans gliding across a calm body of water on a foggy day. The water is still, reflecting the muted colors of the surroundings, and the fog creates a soft, ethereal atmosphere. Initially, two adult swans are seen swimming together, their white feathers contrasting sharply with the grayish-blue water. As the video progresses, more swan cygnets join them, their smaller size and darker plumage making them stand out against the adults. The swans move gracefully, creating gentle ripples in the water as they glide forward. The camera remains steady throughout, focusing on the swans and capturing the tranquil beauty of the moment. The fog adds a layer of mystery to the scene, blurring the background and drawing attention to the swans in the foreground. The overall mood of the video is peaceful and contemplative, highlighting the natural elegance of these birds in their environment.
caption: The video captures a fog-shrouded grey water expanse where an adult white swan floats left of centre and a brown cygnet drifts at its lower left. The swan holds its neck upright through the opening seconds, dark bill forward above a soft reflection. As the clip proceeds the neck bends gradually downward, the head sinking into the body until the swan holds a tucked resting posture that persists in the following frames. A second brown cygnet enters at the right edge early on and drifts leftward to a near halt in the right-central water. A third cygnet later appears at the far right boundary and lingers near the edge. The left cygnet holds its head up early on, then turns it low toward the water. Every bird casts a faint reflection on the calm surface, and the figures appear smaller as the framing widens. The featureless haze offers no landmark, so the birds settle into slow drifting and resting across the grey lake.

review_issues.problem: The left cygnet holds its head up only in the opening frames; from roughly t=1.0s onward it turns its head low so the bill points horizontally at the water, so it does not keep its head raised throughout.

The third cygnet stays pinned to the far-right edge for all of its visible frames; the small inward shift it shows is consistent with the widening framing rather than its own swimming toward the centre.
